q0257.answer: A contingent bill endorsed in favour of a private party is valid only for three months from the date of issue. A bill endorsed on 10-12-2017 and presented on 18-3-2018 is beyond three months, and in any case an endorsement made in the last quarter is valid only up to the end of March. The treasury officer's refusal therefore turns on the three-month limit; the payee must get the bill re-endorsed/revalidated by the drawing officer.

quotes.text: No endorsement on a contingent bill remains valid for longer than three months counting from the date of issue.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 112(c) Endorsement of Contingent Bills in favour of private parties

q0275.answer: Heads of Departments and District Collectors are themselves competent to sanction journeys in the public interest to adjoining districts of neighbouring States. So a District Collector's journey to Coimbatore district needs no separate Government sanction, and the treasury officer was not justified in returning the TA bill on that ground.
q0275.source: KSR Vol I, Part I, Chapter II (TA), Rule 47 Note 2

quotes.text: Note 2.- The Heads of Departments and District Collectors will be competent to undertake journeys outside the State in the adjoining districts of neighbouring States in public interest.
quotes.ref: KSR Vol I, Rule 47 Note 2 (Travelling Allowances, Journeys on Tour)

q0269.answer: A Revised Estimate is an estimate of the probable revenue and expenditure of the current financial year framed during the year. It is based on actual transactions recorded so far plus anticipated transactions for the rest of the year, and should be prepared as realistically as possible because it guides the next year's budget estimate.
q0269.source: Kerala Budget Manual, Chapter II and para 20

quotes.text: Revised estimate is an estimate of the probable revenue and expenditure of the current financial year under the various heads, framed during the course of the year, based on the actual transactions so far recorded and the anticipation for the rest of the year.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Revised Estimate (Chapter II / para 20)

q0365.answer: A muster roll (K.P.W. Form 19) is the record on which wages of departmentally engaged day labourers are drawn and charged to the estimate of the work. One or more rolls are kept for each work, never in duplicate, with separate rolls for each payment period. Daily attendance and absences are recorded in Part I so that net wages can be calculated correctly and tampering is difficult; entries are made in indelible ink.

quotes.text: Muster rolls should be prepared in K.P.W. Form 19 and dealt with in accordance with the following rules:—
One or more muster rolls should be kept for each work, but muster rolls should never be prepared in duplicate .
